# Final Execution Plan

## Wave A — Evidence
Audit canonical dirty files, branch uniqueness vs `origin/main`, worktree dirt, large/untracked/secret-risk files, and patch overlap.

## Wave B — Canonical durability
Make the existing canonical local work durable on `main` without accidentally adding machine-local junk or secrets. Preserve the existing four unique `main` commits.

## Wave C — Remote integration
Merge current `origin/main` into canonical `main`; resolve conflicts with current production truth, full-file source rewrites only, then test affected areas.

## Wave D — Side branch/worktree harvest
For each side branch/worktree: if already contained, remove it; if unique, bring its real work into canonical `main`, test, then remove the branch/worktree. Prune missing worktree metadata.

## Wave E — Main-only product work
Continue the already-designed secure Drive private-content → existing OS opener integration directly in canonical `main`, with no new branches/worktrees.

## Completion gates
- canonical folder only
- branch `main`
- no valuable unique side-branch commits
- no valuable dirty side-worktree state
- no accidental secret/junk commits
- tests green for merged surfaces
- final push is a normal non-force update from canonical `main`
